item.tib: mo 'dul gser sgros dang lcags sgrom gnyis de 'di ni lcags sgroms
item.coloph: ces spa dro stag tshang brag la gter du sbas / kung ston pa zla med gzhon nu / gter nas bton pa yin / mnan bsregs 'phang gsum gzhung dang mthun / bkra shis par gyur cig / / dge'o
item.note: sgros in the title should be read as sgrom; maybe the 'm' has been omitted by mistake or has faded away. We think that kung-ston-pa zla-med gzhon-nu is a name of khu-tsha zla-'od 'bar, not only because of the discovery place (spa-gro being the usual treasure site for khu-tsha), but also for two other reasons: the first is that, according to shar-rdza, he was born in a day of new moon (zla med), the second because his discovery happened when he was 18 years old (which would explain the word gzhon nu, 'youth').
